summary: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Third Higher School and Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He held professorships at Hanazono, Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Kyoto City University of Arts, and visited Harvard.

Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1928 to 1931. He served as a professor at Taisho University (~1968–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1982).

Shingen Takagi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, Gisho Nakano, and Yusho Miyasaka, and served as an assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) of Koyasan University.

Shingo Einoo is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1973–1980) under Wilhelm Rau and held a post at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia from circa 1989 to 2013.

Shingo Enomoto is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who completed a PhD at the University of Marburg (~1973–1980). He held an assistant post at the National Museum of Ethnology from circa 1983 to 1989.

Shinichi Nakazawa is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977), he held academic posts at Chuo University (~1993–2006), Tama Art University (~2006–2011), and Meiji University (~2011–2016).

Shinichi Tsuda is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned a Ph.D. from the Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, later teaching at Eastern Institute and ICPBS.

Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1984–1994). He served at Tottori University (~1995–2000) and was appointed professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2011.

Shinjo Hinonishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He served at Koyasan University as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Supervised by Hajime Nakamura, he studied at the University of Tokyo, lectured at the University at Buffalo, worked at Toyo Bunko, and was a professor at the University of Tsukuba.

Shinjo Suguro was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Tokyo. He served as deputy director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (1980) and as professor at Rissho University (~1970–1996).

Shinjosei Mochizuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923) and Kyoto University (~1923–1926) and held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University.

Shinkai Sugahara was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Waseda University (~1947–1951) and Taisho University (Doctor of Letters, 1991). He served on the faculty at Waseda University (~1962–1972), becoming professor emeritus.

Shinkan Murakami specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at Tohoku University under Nobuo Kumagai, Ensho Kanakura, Ryūjō Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano, later serving as professor at Tohoku University (~1974–1996) and at Seiwa Gakuen College.

Shinko Mochizuki was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928) and Taisho University (1930–1932), where he also held a professorship (~1927–1942).

Shinko Nakai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962–1966) and served as a professor, former president, and professor emeritus at Bukkyo University (~1974–2014).

Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003), teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi (2000), and academic adviser Robert Bickner.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1995. She is attested as a professor at Toyo University in 2015.

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923). He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1959) and held professorships at Toyo University and Kokugakuin University.

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He has held posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
